headline: Guidance improves as losses narrow sequentially
summary_short: Moderna's Q2 2026 revenue was $145M (+2.1% y/y but -62.7% q/q from Q1's $389M), with a GAAP net loss of $782M and EPS of $(1.97) -- a sharp sequential improvement from Q1's $(3.40) loss per share, which included a one-time litigation charge.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue was $145M (+2.1% y/y, well below Q1's $389M which included one-time deliveries), while GAAP net loss narrowed to $782M ($(1.97)/share) from $825M a year ago and $1,343M in Q1. Cost of sales fell 22% y/y on lower unutilized manufacturing capacity costs; R&D fell 7% y/y on wind-down of late-stage programs; SG&A fell 6% on continued cost discipline. Cash and investments were $6.9B at quarter-end, down from $7.5B, after which Moderna paid $950M in July toward its Q1 litigation settlement. Moderna lowered 2026 cost-of-sales and R&D guidance and raised its year-end cash outlook to $4.7-5.2B while reiterating up to 10% revenue growth.

drivers.explanation: CEO Stephane Bancel cited strong execution, pipeline progress, and an improved 2026 operating-expense outlook, framing Q2 as continued momentum ahead of the potential mFLUSIVA approval and key late-2026 oncology and rare-disease readouts.
Lower COVID vaccine sales in the U.S. and South America were offset by UK deliveries under a government partnership and higher stand-ready manufacturing and collaboration revenue, versus Q2 2025.

Cost of sales fell 22% y/y mainly on lower unutilized manufacturing-capacity costs, reflecting continued manufacturing productivity improvements and operational efficiencies; the quarter also included $41M of inventory write-downs.

R&D expenses fell 7% y/y on lower clinical-development costs following the wind-down of several late-stage programs; SG&A fell 6% y/y on continued organizational cost discipline, narrowing the operating loss.
Net loss narrowed largely in line with the operating-income improvement, partly offset by lower interest income ($67M vs $81M) and a swing to a $19M other-expense from an $8M gain a year earlier.

The release attributes the cash decline to funding operations and continued R&D/pipeline investment; Moderna separately disclosed a $950M litigation-settlement payment made in July 2026, after quarter-end, not yet reflected in this balance.
